author: permaculturegeek
body:
I am showing "two years of orna" at level 200, but spent a couple of spells of many months not playing (just checked, playing time = 22 days 8 hours). Based on what I had learned, I levelled an alt character to 151 very fast (61 hours) BUT that character is starved of equipment and resources compared to one which has done the grind out in the world.

Note too, that some of the game content which allows faster levelling is newer additions: Towers and monuments particularly. The pioneering players did it tough.

author: Widogeist
body:
The speed at which you level directly depends on how often you play, access to dungeons, if you're wearing boosting gear to level, and if you party with other players or strictly play solo. An experienced player that knows what gear to upgrade, how/where to farm, etc. could likely hit 250 in under a month. 

Leveling via world raid bosses (summon scrolls) is pretty effective at lower tiers, but once you hit T10 things slow down a lot. T10 is when exp requirements start to scale exponentially. To put things into perspective, it takes roughly the same amount of exp to go from level 241.5-250 as it would to go from level 1-241.5. Around level 241-242 is the *halfway* mark in terms of total exp needed to get to level 250.

Once you hit 225 you'll be able to party with level 250's. 250's don't steal party exp, and if you find someone that runs endless or a lot of dungeons, you can fly through T10 in no time. If you're new to the game I wouldn't really recommend this though. It's important to learn your classes, learn the abilities, and learn the monsters/bosses in each tier and how to fight them. Not only this, but once you hit 250 there's really nothing else to do but min/max gear and grind ascension levels.  

Enjoy the game and have fun, don't worry about rushing to 250.

author: MtPollux
body: I just hit 250 a few days ago, about 13 months after starting my character.  I went through a 2-3 month "dry spell" where I opened the game every day or 2 but didn't do much, so had I played consistently I could have hit 250 in about 10 months.  And I know some have done it faster than that, it depends on how much time you're willing to commit.  Through T9 I got most of my xp from raids, and in T10 it was a combo of raids, towers, and killing world bosses on the highway.  I never really got into endless dungeons, but if I had I would probably have hit 250 much sooner.

author: slapogo
body:
It absolutely does not take years to get to 250. I got to 225 in just under 2 months, and then it was another month or so to get to 250. I certainly played a lot, but I also have a full time job, and spent a lot of time playing other games and doing other things. I believe getting to 225 was done primarily with raids, but the raid xp falls off fast after that, which is when I switched to endless dungeon runs for my primary source of xp.

I will note that I used magic classes to get to tier 8, but after that, I switched to summoner and that sped up leveling up enormously. After I hit tier 10, I abandoned summoner for beowulf, and finally switched to deity, which is my main now.

author: KevineCove
body: I recommend partying up with players that can give you spillover experience and carry you through raids. I power leveled my cousin to 225 in a month and 250 in one more month after that. There are purists that might suggest you get the intended experience but the grind isn't very fun in my opinion.
